legend_note: Colors come from the original SVG legend. Colors repeat across the left and right legend columns, so both color and legend_column matter.

sources_index.arnette_2026: Alan Arnette, Comparing the Routes of Everest, 2026 edition

routes.label: 1924 British (Mallory and Irvine)
routes.note: Mallory and Irvine left high camp above the North Col and disappeared on the Northeast Ridge on 8 June 1924. No summit proof was found, so their final line remains uncertain.

routes.label: 1960 Chinese
routes.note: Wang Fuzhou, Qu Yinhua, and Gonpo reported the first ascent from Tibet on 25 May 1960. Their route followed the North Col, North Ridge, and Northeast Ridge.

routes.label: 1980 Japanese
routes.note: Tsuneo Shigehiro and Takashi Ozaki reached the summit on 10 May 1980 by a direct North Face line through the Japanese and Hornbein couloirs.

routes.label: 1980 Reinhold Messner
routes.note: Reinhold Messner climbed alone from the north side in August 1980, without bottled oxygen, crossing the upper North Face into the Great Couloir before the summit.

routes.label: 1983 American
routes.note: The American team climbed the Kangshung Face from Tibet. Carlos Buhler, Kim Momb, and Louis Reichardt summited on 8 October, followed by Jay Cassell, George Lowe, and Dan Reid the next day.

routes.label: 1984 American
routes.note: Phil Ershler summited on 20 October 1984 after the team used the East Rongbuk-North Col approach, traversed the Central North Face, and joined the Great Couloir.

routes.label: 1984 Australian
routes.note: Tim Macartney-Snape and Greg Mortimer summited on 3 October 1984 by a direct North Face line from the Rongbuk Glacier to the Great Couloir.

routes.label: 1988 International
routes.note: Robert Anderson, Ed Webster, Paul Teare, and Stephen Venables climbed the Neverest Buttress on the Kangshung Face to the South Col. Venables continued to the summit on 12 May 1988.

routes.label: 1995 Japanese
routes.note: A Japanese expedition led by Kanzaki Tadao completed the Northeast Ridge in 1995, climbing through the pinnacled section and rejoining the north-side summit route high on the mountain.

routes.label: 1996 Russian
routes.note: A Russian team led by Sergei Antipin climbed the North-Northeast Couloir in 1996. The new line rose from about 6,400 m to 8,250 m before joining the Northeast Ridge.

routes.label: 1953 British (Hillary and Tenzing)
routes.note: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953 from the South Col and Southeast Ridge. It was the first confirmed ascent of Everest.

routes.label: 1963 American
routes.note: Tom Hornbein and Willi Unsoeld reached the summit on 22 May 1963 by the West Ridge and Hornbein Couloir, then descended by the Southeast Ridge.

routes.label: 1975 British
routes.note: Chris Bonington's expedition climbed the Southwest Face through the Rock Band. Doug Scott and Dougal Haston summited on 24 September 1975 and bivouacked near the South Summit during descent.

routes.label: 1979 Yugoslav
routes.note: The Yugoslav team made the first direct ascent of the West Ridge from the Lho La. Andrej Stremfelj and Jernej Zaplotnik summited on 13 May 1979 and descended by the Hornbein Couloir.

routes.label: 1980 Polish
routes.note: Andrzej Czok and Jerzy Kukuczka reached the summit on 19 May 1980 by the South Pillar, a separate line on the Nepal side of the mountain.

routes.label: 1982 Soviet
routes.note: The first Soviet Everest expedition climbed the left buttress of the Southwest Face in May 1982. Eleven Soviet climbers reached the summit by this route.
